anatomy.flutter: Marker(variant, icon, label) is a single StatelessWidget taking icon as a raw Widget? and label as a plain String — no separate MarkerIcon/MarkerContent classes exist; the icon is sized inline via SizedBox.square(dimension: space(4)) inside Marker.build.
anatomy.web: Marker/MarkerIcon/MarkerContent are three separate exported components — MarkerIcon is aria-hidden="true" with its own size-4 shrink-0 class list, and MarkerContent is a separate <span data-slot="marker-content"> carrying min-w-0 wrap-break-word plus the group-data-[variant=separator]/marker:flex-none / :text-center rules and its own *:[a]:underline link styling.
anatomy.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The Flutter port collapses the web's three-part anatomy (Marker, MarkerIcon, MarkerContent) into one widget with two typed parameters (icon: Widget?, label: String). This forecloses a caller from composing a MarkerContent containing a link — the web's MarkerContent carries *:[a]:underline *:[a]:underline-offset-4 *:[a]:hover:text-foreground specifically for that case, and Marker.dart's own library doc records asChild-and-links as explicitly 'Not ported' (marker.dart:29-30) because 'nothing in the corpus writes one' — but that also means a MarkerContent slot with independent styling/composability does not exist at all, only a bare String.

api.flutter: MarkerVariant enum (normal/separator/border) maps 1:1 onto the cva's variant axis (default/separator/border), with `normal` used in place of the reserved word `default` per the doc comment.
api.web: markerVariants cva declares exactly the same three: default (empty string), separator (before/after rule pseudo-elements), border (border-b border-border pb-2) — no asChild support is exercised by any corpus caller on the Flutter side, matching the doc comment's explicit 'not ported' note for asChild.

states.flutter: Marker is a StatelessWidget with no rest/hover/focus/pressed/disabled branch anywhere in marker.dart — it is a passive annotation row.
states.web: Marker's class list is static aside from the group-data-[variant=separator]/marker: selectors, which key off the variant prop rather than off any interaction state; [a]:hover:text-foreground only applies inside asChild-with-a-link, which the doc comment records as unreached by the ported corpus.
states.note: A Marker is inert decoration/annotation on both platforms in the shape the corpus actually builds — no interactive state exists to compare beyond the unreached asChild+link hover, which neither side builds.

disabled.flutter: No enabled/disabled parameter exists in marker.dart.
disabled.web: markerVariants declares no disabled: variant either.
disabled.note: A Marker reports a fact about surrounding content ('Today', 'Context cleared') — it is never itself an operable control, so disabled does not apply on either platform.

interaction.flutter: No GestureDetector, Focus, or MouseRegion anywhere in Marker.build — the row accepts no input.
interaction.web: Marker adds no onClick/tabIndex of its own; any interactivity would come only from an asChild <a>, which is explicitly unbuilt on the Flutter side and the doc comment notes is absent from the corpus on the web side too.
interaction.note: Marker is non-interactive on both platforms in every shape the current corpus actually renders.

semantics.flutter: No explicit Semantics wrapping is added — the row's plain StyledText children are read by whatever ambient semantics Flutter attaches to text, and MarkerIcon-equivalent icons are passed in directly with no aria-hidden translation since the Dart port has no separate MarkerIcon class to carry one.
semantics.web: MarkerIcon renders aria-hidden="true" explicitly (marker.tsx:72) so the glyph is never announced, leaving only MarkerContent's text read — the label is the whole of the accessible content on both platforms even though the Flutter side reaches that outcome by never building a discrete icon wrapper rather than by hiding one.
